reduction_summary: For the exact-rank-three heavy near-null state with r0=sqrt(c)e1, c>1/2, rho=1-c, M=[[eta,b,0],[b,alpha,delta],[0,delta,gamma]], define L=eta sqrt(rho) T+bV and B_eta=[[alpha-b^2/eta,delta],[delta,gamma]]. Exact completion gives Q=c eta (X0+L/(sqrt(c)eta))^2+(V,W)^T B_eta(V,W), with det(B_eta)=det(M)/eta. Thus eta det(B_eta)=det M and spectral curvature does not degenerate as eta tends to zero. The residual product projection has det Gram(L,V,W)=eta^2 rho, but det Gram(L,W)=b^2+eta^2 rho; for |eta|<=1/2, sigma_min(M)>=1 implies |b|>=sqrt(3)/2 and hence ||p_(L,W)||inf<=4/sqrt(3). The remaining bridge must use this good two-dimensional pair while retaining the same-source V coordinate.
new_obstruction_summary: For every fixed 1<=p<2 there is no law-uniform bound on int|fhat|^p over probability densities f<=1. The lacunary indicator f_N of union_[k=1]^N [2^k,2^k+1/N] has Fourier factor a_N D_N; |a_N|>=c/N on |xi|<=N, E|D_N|^2=N, E|D_N|^4=2N^2-N, and Paley-Zygmund yields int|fhat_N|^p >= C_p N^(1-p/2). Since normalized BL leverage is invariant under invertible active-coordinate changes, a heavy row of leverage c>1/2 forces forbidden exponent 1/c<2 in the direct geometric three-square absolute-Fourier route.

required_claude_source.application: Its p>=2 cap-one Fourier lemma is used at the exact heavy-row threshold; the new lacunary theorem proves that a fixed p<2 extension is false. Its ruled theorem still pays the majority-sign one-sheet side by pi sqrt(2).

partner_result.application: The scoped raw-diagonal fresh-square theorem gives ||p_Q||inf<581.745 for m>=3/20, mu>=1, delta_B>=1/16; no transfer outside its ratio-packet hypotheses is asserted.

predecessor.application: Provides the uniformly paid eta=0 endpoint and motivates the punctured near-null bridge.

already_known_not_new: The near-coloop capped-basis entropy barrier was already proved by account02/B16; this run proves a distinct sub-L2 Fourier obstruction to feeding the heavy row directly into geometric absolute Fourier/BL.
next_step: Prove a rough interval/coarea receiver using the uniformly transverse product pair (L,W) while retaining V in the same original-coordinate product bank. The theorem must remain uniform in eta,rho and avoid positive conditional density moments/caps for V|(L,W) and unrestricted curved-fiber suprema.
